title: Indoor Skydiving for Kids: What It’s Like and What to Know
description: Indoor skydiving for kids and teens explained: how the wind tunnel works, minimum ages, what to wear, how long you fly and why it makes a great experience gift.
h1: Indoor skydiving for kids and teens
intro: Fly like a superhero, no plane required. Indoor skydiving uses a vertical wind tunnel to float you on air, and it’s surprisingly kid-friendly.

image.alt: Hot air balloons rising over the landscape

cardText: How the wind tunnel works, ages, flight time and what to wear.

blocks.title: Scout’s flying tip
blocks.text: Flights are short (often a minute or two each), but it feels much longer. Buy two flights if you can: the second is when it clicks.
points: Check minimum age and weight rules
Arrive early for the training briefing

sections.html: Fans blow air up a tall glass tunnel fast enough to lift you. You wear a flight suit, helmet and goggles, and an instructor flies alongside you, holding and guiding you.
Centres set minimum ages and maximum weights, and some have height rules. Many welcome young children with an instructor. Check your centre’s rules before booking.
It’s a pricier treat, so it makes a great experience gift or birthday day out. Find it in our adventure parks guide.

faqs.q: Is indoor skydiving safe for kids?
faqs.a: It’s supervised by trained instructors who fly with you. Centres set age, weight and health rules, so check them before booking.
